result.summary: Enhances the torcontrol fuzz harness to drive TorControlConnection through a mocked socket (DynSock) rather than directly invoking callbacks with short dummy strings. It generates well-formed cryptographic replies (v3 onion IDs, SAFECOOKIE challenge hashes, valid private keys), raises reply line limits from 16 to 256 bytes, and asserts outgoing command formatting. It also fixes a bug in DynSock::Wait() where wrapping this in an owning shared_ptr caused premature socket destruction.
result.problem: The existing torcontrol fuzz target feeds fabricated lines capped at 16 characters directly to callbacks, completely bypassing wire parsing in ProcessBuffer and ReceiveAndProcess as well as authentication success paths. In addition, calling DynSock::Wait() deleted the underlying socket due to an owning shared_ptr temporary.
evidence: PR description reports line coverage of src/torcontrol.cpp jumps from 52.2% to 81.8% and branch coverage from 47.5% to 74.0% with the new harness.
Commit 345ffe0dae identifies and fixes an existing bug in test helper DynSock::Wait() introduced in #30205 that deleted the socket on return.
result.scope_notes: Changes the input format for the torcontrol fuzz target, requiring a refreshed corpus in bitcoin-core/qa-assets.
result.card: This PR upgrades the torcontrol fuzz target to route traffic through a mocked DynSock and construct valid Tor control values (such as v3 onion IDs and SAFECOOKIE HMACs) with replies up to 256 bytes. Previously, the fuzzer called TorController callbacks directly with short strings, missing wire buffer parsing and almost all success paths. The PR also fixes an existing bug in DynSock::Wait() that destroyed the socket instance on call return. Author measurements show line coverage of torcontrol.cpp increasing from 52.2% to 81.8% and branch coverage from 47.5% to 74.0%.

risk.why: Touches only fuzz harness code and test utilities, with no impact on production node behavior.
